title: validQuantity accepts empty, blank, negative, zero, fractional and Infinity quantities
evidence: isNaN coerces its string argument with Number(). Number("") and Number("  ") are 0; "-5", "0", "1.5", "1e3" and "Infinity" are all numbers. app.js:19 uses it as the only quantity check; app.js:20 then stores Number(qtyText) and app.js:10 multiplies it into the total.
failing_case: Leave Quantity blank, price 10, click Add line: a line with qty 0 is added. Quantity -3 with price 10 adds a line and the total becomes -30.00. Quantity Infinity gives a total of Infinity.
remediation: Validate with a pure function that requires a trimmed, non-empty string that parses to a finite integer >= 1, add a unit test per rejected shape, and use it for the stored value too.

title: tooSoon never trips: lastSend is never set, so double-send protection does nothing
evidence: Grep of both scripts: lastSend is declared at guards.js:22 and read at guards.js:24, and assigned nowhere. It stays 0, so Date.now() - 0 is about 1.7e12, which is never < 1000. app.js:25 relies on the guard, and the send button is not disabled while the request is in flight (app.js:24-29).
failing_case: Double-click Send invoice. Both clicks pass tooSoon() and each posts the full lines array to /api/invoices, so the invoice is created twice.
remediation: Disable the button (or hold an `inFlight` flag) from click until the response settles and send an idempotency key. If a time guard is kept, set lastSend = Date.now() when the send starts.

title: canVoid is inverted: every non-admin may void, the only admin may not
evidence: Array.prototype.indexOf returns -1 when the item is absent and 0 when it is first. -1 is truthy, 0 is falsy. app.js:2 defines the signed-in user as roles ["viewer", "billing"]; app.js:32 gates the void button on canVoid(user). Traced by hand; I could not run node in this workspace (Bash was denied).
failing_case: user.roles = ["viewer","billing"] -> indexOf = -1 -> truthy -> canVoid returns true, so the request to /api/invoices/void is sent. user.roles = ["admin"] -> indexOf = 0 -> falsy -> canVoid returns false, so the admin is blocked. ["viewer","admin"] works only by accident (index 1).
remediation: Use `return user.roles.includes("admin");` and add a test for no roles, admin first, admin later, and no admin. Enforce the same rule on the server.

quote: const user = { name: "sam", roles: ["viewer", "billing"] };  // the signed-in user
title: Role is a hard-coded client object and the only void check is in the browser
evidence: The roles come from a literal in client code, and canVoid (guards.js:9) is the only gate visible in the payload. Anyone can call fetch("/api/invoices/void", {method:"POST"}) from the console. The server is not in the payload, so server-side enforcement is unconfirmed.
failing_case: In devtools: `user.roles.push("admin")` or a direct fetch POST to /api/invoices/void. If the server trusts the request, any viewer voids invoices.
remediation: Read the user from the session on the server, enforce the void permission there, and treat the client check as a UI hint only.

title: Each line renders its client name as a link that goes nowhere
evidence: The anchor has href="#", no handler and no action. It adds a tab stop per line with a title that repeats the visible text.
failing_case: Keyboard user tabs to a client name and presses Enter: the URL gains `#` and the page may jump to the top, with no other effect. A screen reader announces "link" for something that does nothing.
remediation: Render the client as plain text, or make it a real link or button that does something; drop the duplicate title.

quote: const total = lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.qty * l.price, 0);
title: Displayed unit price is rounded but the total uses the unrounded price
evidence: app.js:19 accepts any positive number for price. render() shows l.price.toFixed(2) (app.js:8) and totals with the raw l.price (app.js:10). Money is also summed as floating point.
failing_case: Add price 0.004, quantity 1000. The line reads `1000 × 0.00` but Total shows 4.00. The invoice on screen does not add up.
remediation: Store prices as integer minor units, reject more than 2 decimals at the boundary, and compute line and invoice totals from those integers in one tested function.

title: Invalid quantity or price is dropped silently; the form just does nothing
evidence: The submit handler returns with no message, no aria-live text, no focus move and no aria-invalid. Quantity and price inputs have no `required` or type (index.html:16,18), so native validation does not step in either.
failing_case: Type price `1,50` (decimal comma, a common locale) or `abc`, and click Add line. Number("1,50") is NaN, the handler returns, and the user sees no line added and no reason why. Screen-reader users get no signal at all.
remediation: On rejection show an inline error beside the field ("Price must be a number above 0, e.g. 1.50"), set aria-invalid and move focus to the first bad field; accept or normalise the locale decimal.

quote: const res = await fetch("/api/invoices", { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(lines) });
title: fetch rejection is not caught: offline or failed requests give the user no message
evidence: Only `!res.ok` is handled (app.js:27). fetch rejects on network failure, DNS failure or abort, and the async click handler has no try/catch. The same pattern is at app.js:33.
failing_case: Go offline and click Send invoice (or Void invoice). The promise rejects as an unhandled rejection in the console; the user sees nothing and cannot tell whether the invoice was sent, so they click again.
remediation: Wrap each request in try/catch/finally, show the same visible error for a thrown fetch as for !res.ok, and restore the button state in finally.

title: An empty invoice can be sent
evidence: The send handler checks only tooSoon() (app.js:25), never lines.length.
failing_case: Open the page and click Send invoice straight away. POST /api/invoices is sent with body `[]`, creating (or erroring on) an empty invoice.
remediation: Disable Send until lines.length > 0, and reject empty bodies on the server.

title: A successful send is invisible and leaves the sent lines in place
evidence: After a 2xx response the handler only increments sentCount, which is never read anywhere in the payload. There is no success message, the list is not cleared, and the button has no sending state. A successful void (app.js:34) is also silent.
failing_case: Add lines, click Send invoice. Nothing on screen changes. The user cannot tell success from a dead button, and a second click re-posts the same lines.
remediation: Show a status message in an aria-live region ("Invoice sent"), clear or lock the lines, disable the button while sending, and drop or use sentCount.

title: Void is a one-click irreversible action with no confirmation and no invoice identified
evidence: The click handler posts straight away with no body naming an invoice. In index.html:23-24 the Void button sits directly beside Send with the same style (styles.css:4 gives all buttons the same look).
failing_case: A mis-click on Void, next to Send invoice, voids with no confirm or undo. The request carries no invoice id, so which invoice is voided is up to the server's session state.
remediation: Send the invoice id in the request, require a confirm step that names the invoice, and give Void a distinct destructive style away from Send.

title: escapeHtml does not escape quotes, so the title="..." attribute in render() can be broken out of
evidence: app.js:8 puts escapeHtml(l.client) inside a double-quoted attribute (title="..."). escapeHtml leaves " untouched. The result is assigned through innerHTML at app.js:7. The client field is free text (index.html:14).
failing_case: Enter client = `x" onmouseover="alert(document.domain)` and add a line. The rendered markup is `<a href="#" title="x" onmouseover="alert(document.domain)">`, and the handler runs on hover. Impact is held at High, not Critical, because the string comes from the user's own input and is not stored; it becomes Critical if client names are ever pasted from, or loaded from, another source.
remediation: Escape " and ' in escapeHtml (" '), or build the list with createElement/textContent and setAttribute so no value is ever parsed as HTML.
fix: not offerable: unbalanced brackets or quotes
